Can schizophrenia dull your pain receptors. triggering stuff about self harm and intense delusions ahead, keep yourself safe please When I was 17 and very delusional I had an incident where the TV told me that Id had a tracking device planted in my arm while I was asleep, so a few nights later I used a razor blade to dig through my arm to try and find it. I have an extensive history with self harm, but this was one of the only cases where it was done as a direct result of a psychotic episode, and one thing I noticed was that I felt no pain whatsoever. Every other time Ive self harmed there has been pain, even just a slight sting for a few seconds, but this incident, which had me going deeper than almost any other incident, had no pain. I wasnt sure what to think of it but a few months later when I was recounting the incident to my psychiatrist he specifically asked if I felt any pain during it, which makes me wonder now if the psychotic brain can completely shut off your ability to feel pain? Is this something anyone else has experienced, and is there any studies that have looked into this, because Im quite curious now.

A poem about depression. My Tormentor, Depression You take me down to the depths And leave me there, halfconscious and bare In your grasp. How strong are you really? Not very. I know youre weak But you sneak up behind me And attack when I least suspect you. When that happens, I dont want to fight. I want to lose I want you to take me. And that is why you always win. You take away from me happiness and sadness alike Make me indifferent between good and bad Even rob me of my will to live. To you I yield my tormentor. I am at your mercy. What do you want from me? How much deeper will you take me? Suddenly, you let me go, and I swim to the surface I gasp and breathe in the air of hope, and just for a moment I think that maybe everything is going to be okay. Then you grab my leg, and pull me back down You show me hope only to take it away from me Only to make my suffering worse To you I yield, my tormentor.

Episodes of Atypical Depression vs Episodes of Major Depressive Disorder ELI5. My understanding 1. Accepting my situation. Acceptance is not that you will accept what happened and move on. Thats too easy. Acceptance happens when you become so helpless to that feeling that you make it part of you. You accept that no matter where you are or what you do, that feeling will be there. Like an embarrassing pain that you cant verbalize. Until one day you can move on sometimes it is hours, sometimes its days, weeks, months, years. but when you finally move on there will be reminders and youll feel a sting but it will be so distant that you wont remember the initial pain. Use a notebook to boost your selfesteem and learn how to be positive. At the begining of 2018 I decided to do this activity. I had this cool notebook to which I occasionally wrote my thoughts when I was feeling down. I figured it would be nice to fill it up so I decided to fixate every momment that gave me positive emotions or simply something that I should be proud of. I write a date and make it into a simple sentance like I did not feel as anxious as I used to be in a particular situation or today I had a decent conversation with someone and feeling a bit awkward did not ruin it. Maybe something like I really enjoyed watching this new movie Ive been waiting for. It could be I really enjoyed my alone time today from all the people. Of course if you want you can make it into whole paragraph. Anyway, that way I learned that finding good things in life is actually quite easy. Even when it feels like nothing much is going on at the momment. I dont look at it as false positivity because all of the things I write are true. In fact, most of the negative things I told myself before were irrational and not true. I learned what small things make me happy and I focus on them. Get yourself a cool notebook and make it your positivity journal. Whenever you feel an emotion which leans to the good side, remember it and write it down in the evening before you go to bed. Once you fill it up, you can read it when you feel down to remember those momments that made you feel good about yourself.

Having constricted breathinginability to catch your breathfeeling like you cant fill your lungs? Read THIS. Anyway if youve tried breathing techniques, tried all the naturalistic ways of treating it and nothing is working then hear me out Today I talked to my doctor and she had no problem prescribing me a salbutamol ventolin inhaler. Its a really quick release from the constrictedlimited breathing you typically feel with anxiety and the feeling of inability to catch your breathfill you lungs. I have only used it once and it works AMAZING. So far one use has lasted me a few hours still going and all my anxiety from breathing feels suddenly lifted. Also my prescription which came with 200 uses with a max of 2 uses per day, so this is a somewhat longterm solution. I am also on a few other things for anxietydepression but at this point I almost feel I dont need them because I have finally gotten control of my breathing. Anyway hope this helps, dont be afraid to talk to your doctors, people!

A diagnosis that helped me. I was about 18 when I started to notice symptoms that really started to affect my functioning. At first it was a lethargy. Then it moved on to being so completely lazy that I would rather be hungry than walk the 1.5 miles for free university food. Eventually, the RA of our dorm knocked on my door to see if I was still alive. I dropped out of college soon after and had very little plan to keep living. For about 2 years I ran through the same process. I would go see a doc, he would tell me I was depressed a prescribe antidepressants and recommend me to a psychiatrist. After the first session, the shrink would declare I was not depressed and should see a different doctor. This went on for years, all the while, I was asking each of them if it wasnt that I was so tired because I was depressed, but that I was depressed because I was so tired. Never! I was depressed and we just hadnt found the right drug! Finally, after about three years, I had a doc look at me with a confused expression and say, Huh, I never thought of it that way! She signed me up for a sleep study, and it turned out I was narcoleptic. A year later I went in to see her for a sinus infection and she actually thanked me. Since then she had given sleep studies to many patients that didnt respond to traditional meds and found they had sleep disorders. tldr Find doctors who actually listen to you and you trust, and maybe look into other causes like sleep disorders. Edit before I even post 20 years later my sleeping is managed but not great, and now do suffer from actual depression.

It Gets Better. I was diagnosed with depression 10 years ago when I was 14 years old. I still battle depression, over the years it has manifested itself in the form of Chronic Pain. There are daysphases I dont want to leave the house or speak to anyone, and there is always that lingering hopelessness in the back of my mind almost sneering at my life as if to say Whats the point?. I choose to battle that feeling every day. Some days it wins, most days I do. The most important tool I use in that fight is identifying then separating depression from my other emotionsthought processes. Once I have labeled a feeling or thought process as Depression, I write it off and actively stop my mind from entertaining it. Ive been training my mind this way since I was 14 and for me it works. I know we all experience different forms and levels of depression, but keeping hope is universal to all of us. It will take time, effort and willpower but you can do it. Just because you didnt get out of bed yesterday, doesnt mean you cant absolutely nail that sales pitch or go talk to that girl. You are stronger than you know.

Below is a theory about why this is. I had spoken to my psychology professor at college after learning about rumination in her class. I told her that I had a theory that the reason memory and thinking issues may have transpired from the depression was because of rumination. Rumination is when you focus on negative events and go over and over it in your head. So I thought my brain must have protected itself against this by shrinking my hippocampus, making it more difficult to recall these negative memories, but this also made it more difficult to recall all other memories as well. I had almost eidetic memory before this illness got me, and it frustrates me to hell that Im unable to think the way I used to. My Small Tip for Dealing with Invasive Suicidal Thoughts. Ive dealt with invasive suicidal and selfharm related thoughts my whole life, ever since I can remember. I was diagnosed with depression pretty quickly and my first therapist tried to teach me to banish my thoughts to keep me from spiraling. This ended up just making me feel worse because I felt guilty for having thoughts I shouldnt and it just ended up contributing to the selfhate. I ended up eventually exploring meditation and specifically how meditation handles the mental chatter really helped me deal with my invasive thoughts. You try to clear your mind and if the thoughts come up, you acknowledge them, respond to them, but then let them pass. Its ok if it takes a while or if the thoughts dont totally go away, it takes practice to clear your mind and let the thoughts go. You also have to acknowledge that the end you are seeking to the thoughts wont come. They will always be there and learning to live with them and acknowledge them is the best way to deal with them. After months of practicing this I was able to live a lot calmer and at peace life. I didnt feel like I was at war with my depression anymore and it was honestly gratifying. Im going to be sad. Theres nothing I can do to change that. But I can stay alive and unharmed physically. I got away from the practice for several years due to many life changes but am coming back and relearning it. It takes a while to get into but it can help some people so much. Just thought Id share something that has helped me. This is of course, not a replacement for therapy, medication, or any other treatment.

Medication Saved My Life 17 Years After Diagnosis. Ive tried almost every antidepressant out there since I was diagnosed in 2001 MDD. Have been hospitalized 3x for self harm, and almost went back last summer. Only hesitated because I dont have insurance. My PTSD had been seriously triggered and I spent 2 weeks constantly panicking and fantasizing about ending my life. A couple days in, convinced family to get me to a free mental health clinic. The dr there added Effexor which I had taken before tolerated well to my Wellbutrin. It took about 2 weeks for it to kick in, but once it did, I was so relieved. I havent even gone down the road toward the feelings that lead to self harm in the past year. I feel so lucky. Im so relieved not to be feeling low. I still have anxiety and fatigue, and I guess the sort of overall pessimistic outlook that depression gives people isnt something that just goes away. I mean, once youve been there, youve been there, I guess. But I just cant even imagine feeling down that way again. Also, I guess Im aware that this may change at some point, since I do have significant comorbidities such as PTSD, GAD, ADHD. But its also such a relief, because of those conditions, to have a break from the unrelenting depression for a while. I guess I just want to share that it is possible to find something that helps, even if youve been searching for years. Free mental health clinics save lives. Psychiatrists that dont seem really interested or compassionate can save lives. Cheap generic meds save lives. Combinations of meds save lives.

Yesterday was 4 years. My dad was diagnosed nearly 10 years ago with frontal lobe dementia. I was only 16 at the time, though we think he probably had been sick for most of my life. Fast forward 6 years and he wasnt able to stay home by himself anymore and my mom who is an elementary school teacher had to hire a nurse to stay with him during the day until the time came he needed to go to a nursing home. His mind was so far gone that he didnt know what was going on, but he kept trying to escape the nursing home. They ended up sending him to a hospital to try to find a way to calm him down. Someone at the hospital decided to pump him full of drugs that you arent supposed to give an elderly dementia patient, and he ended up dying a week later at 64. I was 22 and in my last semester of college when he died. We had an autopsy performed and Lewy Body was confirmed. The last real conversation with him was the summer before when I had to buy a new car. He was mad that I didnt include him, but then was mad that I was paying for it myself and we went around in circles. The next time I saw him was Thanksgiving and he had no idea what was going on. Its strange how you can hate someone so much during life, but start being upset that theyre gone years later. TLDR My dad died from Lewy Body dementia 4 years ago.

Depression is SEVERELY underestimated. The fact that depression is considered the common cold of mental illnesses is a problem. In my opinion, depression is the worst possible thing that can happen to someone. Being diagnosed with terminal cancer, contracting AIDS, even losing all of your limbs for whatever reason are all better fates that depression because while afflicted with those conditions, you still have the possibility of experiencing positive emotional states. When youre truly depressed, there is no chance of feeling anything meaningful, joyful or good, and that is a fate worse than death. Of course, those conditions suck ass and increase the likelihood of developing depression. Regardless, I dont think the majority of people can comprehend the sheer magnitude of the disease, and the profound changes that depression induces in ones experience of life.

The likeness between Depression and Dark Souls 2. You are truly alone in this world, in the sense that no one can help you till the end but yourself. Sure, you might get assistance from NPCs and other players, but if you arent ready or cant get to a certain place based on your own capabilities, its your own incompetence. No Pressure. You get to see other depressed individuals struggling in their ghost forms around you, watch their mistakes and hope that you dont repeat them. Theres a sense of community despite the isolation, you are fighting your own battle, but others serve as a reminder for you, and you do the same for them. Dying and losing currency souls is stressful and crushing, especially if youre unable to retrieve it upon revival. This reminds us that failure is costly, and you only have one chance to make things right before all your efforts go to waste. Sounds fatalistic, but I assume its the mentality of most depressed individuals. Dont screw up, dont screw up, dont screw up. I screwed up, despite the loss, most of us would trudge along, albeit painfully, what compels us? The answer is within yourself. The punishing environment, the brutality of autosave. Theres no turning back in Dark Souls, just like real life, you cant afford to be like wonder what happens if I do this? perhaps you can if youve stocked up on souls, human effigy and the safetyrings I thought about these points while having a shower. Lemme know what you peeps think. Also, like everything else Ive written thus far, this is my opinion.

This disorder is rough. You can be stable for so long, and then something can trigger you and you lose control. Ive been doing well. I have a lot of big life changes happening, and Ive been able to roll with it, but the other day I was completely triggered. I was late for a counseling group, and being emotional like we are, I could read the emotions of my counselor disappointment, frustration, coldness. I couldnt sit with how that made me feel angry, stressed, confused. My thoughts I left at the time I always do, it isnt my fault there was crazy traffic. Why is she making me feel like shit? I am not a child. But this disorder can often cause us to react like children, like someone whose emotions are unstable or underdeveloped. So I tried to come up with a list of truths, and I wanted to share. 1. I am not a victim. I am responsible for the choices that I make. 2. I have a duty to the people around me. My work, my counselor, my children. Duties must be fulfilled. 3. It does not benefit anyone for me to act out. I must breathe. I must remain calm. 4. I cannot control someone elses emotions. Yeah, my counselor was being a bit of a cold bitch. But I let it stop me from completing group for the day because I freaked out and left. 5. I am strong enough to sit with uncomfortable emotions. Life is not a storybook that I can flip to the end of. I am on this page. Focus on this page.

Depression does not discriminate. You dont need a reason to be depressed. Nothing bad has to happen. It is a medical condition, and imbalance of chemicals in your brain. Your sadness and pain is all valid. If you take medication for it you be probably heard peoples dismissive comments about the side effects or how you just need to exercise and eat your veggies. But the honest truth is that there is something wrong with you. And while there is something wrong with you is not abnormal, you are not alone and please dont make yourself do this alone. Your brain is a lump of meat sitting in chemical soup, of course its going to get confused sometimes and send out the wrong signals or none at all. Just like you take medication for blood pressure or diabetes antidepressants, antianxiety, and antipsychotics are all valid medications. People who have depression and anxiety are often seen as weaker, when in reality it is entirely the opposite. They are the strongest, most empathetic people. Please do not be ashamed to get help. And if you ever need anything, just to talk or whatever, Im here. Ive been through this journey, im still on it. But im out of the deep and im seeing the bright side, and I really want everyone around to see it with me. I love you.
